items.headline: Warsh turns Jackson Hole into a real tightening signal: inflation remains the predominant policy focus
items.category: Macro / Federal Reserve / Rates / Capital Allocation
items.summary: Chair Kevin Warsh said the Fed must be confident that underlying inflation is moving clearly and sufficiently fast toward 2%; otherwise policymakers still have work to do. He described labor markets as broadly consistent with full employment, inflation progress as modest and financial conditions as showing few signs of restraint. Rate futures moved to roughly a 56–60% probability of a September hike from about 35–40% before the speech.
items.whyItMatters: This is a substantive change from yesterday's event-risk posture. The policy distribution has shifted hawkishly, raising the hurdle rate for long-duration equities, Treasuries, leveraged real estate and other rate-sensitive assets. AGCI keeps duration staggered, liquidity intact and requires stronger valuation support before adding beta.
items.agciSignal: FED HAWKISH SHIFT / HIGHER HURDLE RATE / KEEP LIQUIDITY

items.headline: AI capex remains structurally powerful, but the investment case is moving from TAM growth to return on capital
items.summary: Barron's new weekend cover asks whether the AI capex boom is becoming a bubble and frames the cycle against long market history. The material investment takeaway is not that the cycle is ending now, but that unusually large infrastructure spending eventually requires proof of utilization, pricing power, monetization and free-cash-flow conversion.
items.whyItMatters: Nvidia has confirmed demand, but the next phase of the AI trade should discriminate between companies funding growth from durable cash generation and those relying on increasingly expensive external capital. AGCI raises the weight of ROIC, FCF after capex and balance-sheet resilience in AI selection.
items.agciSignal: AI STRUCTURAL / ROIC AND FCF > NARRATIVE

items.headline: Stocks weaken while the dollar and front-end Treasury yields rise after Warsh
items.summary: Global equities weakened in choppy trade after Warsh's speech, while the dollar and short-dated Treasury yields rose. The two-year yield increased more than the long end as markets repriced the near-term Fed path toward a higher probability of a September hike.
items.whyItMatters: The cross-asset reaction confirms that the speech changed the market's policy distribution rather than merely its rhetoric. A flatter/higher front end argues for more caution in duration, growth multiple expansion and leveraged carry trades.
items.agciSignal: CROSS-ASSET HAWKISH CONFIRMATION / DO NOT CHASE DURATION

items.headline: Hormuz remains operationally constrained despite diplomacy; crude ends lower but chokepoint risk is unresolved
items.summary: Only seven commodity vessels transited Hormuz on Thursday versus 17 the prior day and a 10-day average of 15. Oil nevertheless settled lower on Friday and posted a weekly loss as markets weighed Fed tightening risk and speculation about a possible navigation deal.
items.whyItMatters: The energy tail risk has not disappeared: physical traffic remains impaired even as price pressure eases. AGCI keeps a moderate hedge rather than expanding it, while monitoring shipping normalization because a renewed disruption would feed directly into inflation and the Fed reaction function.
items.agciSignal: PHYSICAL RISK PERSISTS / MODERATE HEDGE / NO OIL CHASE

items.headline: Gulf states accelerate pipelines and ports designed to bypass Hormuz
items.summary: The prolonged Iran conflict is accelerating Gulf investment in pipelines, Red Sea and eastern-UAE ports, and other infrastructure intended to reduce dependence on Hormuz. The shift is strategic rather than tactical and reflects an assumption that chokepoint risk can remain structurally elevated.
items.whyItMatters: For AGCI, this creates a longer-duration real-asset theme in logistics, pipelines, ports and related infrastructure while reinforcing that the geopolitical risk premium should not be assumed to vanish even if oil prices temporarily fall.
